case_title: Monica Bedi v. State of A.P.
statutory_provisions: IPC s. 120-B, 419, 420, 468; Prevention of Corruption Act s. 13(1)(d) r/w 13(2)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under sections 120-B, 419 and 420 IPC; acquitted under Section 12 of the Passports Act, 1967
neutral_facts: The accused, Monica Bedi, entered into a conspiracy with other individuals to secure a passport in the assumed name of 'SM' by submitting false documents. The passport was used to travel abroad, and the accused faced prosecution and conviction in Portugal. In India, the accused and others were charged under various provisions of the Penal Code and the Prevention of Corruption Act. The trial court convicted the accused under sections 120-B, 419, and 420 IPC but acquitted her of the charge under Section 12 of the Passports Act, 1967. The High Court confirmed the conviction but modified the sentence. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction, reducing the sentence to the period already undergone while maintaining the fine amount.
